application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: Hanyang University International Graduate Admissions Portal & StudyinKorea Portal
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the Hanyang OIA online application portal during the application window (September-October for Spring; March-April for Fall), complete personal details, upload required documents, and submit before deadline.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1 (August - September for Spring / January - February for Fall): Explore Hanyang CS faculty lab websites and email prospective professors with CV and research statement.
Step 2 (Online portal): Access the Hanyang University International Graduate Admissions online portal.
Step 3 (Complete application): Fill out application form, select target degree program, and indicate prospective lab supervisor (if contacted).
Step 4 (Upload documents): Upload certified PDF scans of transcripts, degree certificates, study plan, CV, 2 recommendation letters, and English certificate / MOI letter.
Step 5 (Fee payment): Pay KRW 138,000 application fee online and submit.
Step 6 (Faculty review & interview): College of Computing admissions committee reviews dossiers and may conduct virtual interviews.
Step 7 (Admission & HISP announcement): Admission decision and HISP scholarship award notification released simultaneously on the portal.
Step 8 (Certificate of Admission): Formally accept offer, receive Certificate of Admission (CoA), and apply for Korean D-2 Student Visa.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated automatic consideration: All international applicants are automatically evaluated for the HISP scholarship based on their application dossier; no separate scholarship application required.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Two academic recommendation letters uploaded directly to the admissions portal or submitted by referees via automated links.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Study Plan / Statement of Purpose: (1) Motivations for choosing Hanyang University, (2) Previous academic and research achievements, (3) Detailed study and research plan in target field, (4) Future career goals.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Structured 2 to 3-page study plan detailing research interests, technical tools, and prospective lab alignment.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic CV detailing education, programming proficiencies, research publications, and capstone projects.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Some faculty lab PIs conduct a 20-30 minute virtual technical interview via Zoom to evaluate coding proficiency and research background before confirming lab placement.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic (6.0+), TOEFL iBT (80+), or English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate. GRE is NOT required.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Notarized or apostilled degree certificates and transcripts uploaded; HEC attestation and MOFA attestation required for Pakistani credentials.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Notarized English translations required for all non-English documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: 100% digital submission via the Hanyang International Graduate Admissions portal.

fake_websites_and_scams: Commercial education recruiters charging large sums claiming guaranteed admission or scholarships at Hanyang. Applications are processed strictly via oia.hanyang.ac.kr.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Hanyang application fee is KRW 138,000 paid online directly to the university. Never pay fees to external agents.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Hanyang works with authorized recruitment agencies for undergraduate admissions, but graduate research placements are handled directly by professors. Never pay agents for scholarship placement.
hidden_costs_breakdown: Application fee: KRW 138,000 (~PKR 29,000).
Korean D-2 Student Visa fee: USD 60 (~PKR 17,000).
Flight ticket from Pakistan to Seoul: ~PKR 200,000 to 320,000.
First month's dorm deposit and living costs: ~KRW 600,000 (~PKR 126,000).
misleading_claims_debunked: CLAIM: You must take TOPIK (Korean language test). (FACT: 100% of graduate computing courses and research in Computer Software are in English; TOPIK is not required).
CLAIM: The HISP scholarship covers living expenses. (FACT: The HISP scholarship covers tuition fees only; living stipends are provided separately by your research lab professor via BK21/NRF grants).
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Some online blogs state that HISP renewal requires a 4.0 GPA. In fact, maintaining the HISP scholarship requires maintaining a minimum GPA of 3.00 on a 4.0 scale each semester.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must maintain cumulative GPA of 3.00 / 4.00 or higher each semester to retain the HISP tuition waiver for the following semester.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: No clawback of previously awarded funds; semester GPA falling below 3.0 results in loss of tuition waiver for subsequent term.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Changing department requires formal approval from both departments.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Master's scholarship capped at 2 years; PhD scholarship capped at 4 years. Professor funding can continue beyond.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: CSC Online Application System (Agency No. 10284) & NJU International Student Portal
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the CSC portal selecting 'Program Category Type B', input NJU Agency Number '10284'. Concurrently register on the NJU International Student Service System and upload matching documentation.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Explore NJU faculty profiles and reach out to prospective supervisors with CV and research abstract (October - December).
Step 2: Secure the formal NJU 'Provisional Acceptance Letter for International Students' signed by the professor and school.
Step 3: Complete CSC online registration under Type B (Agency No. 10284) and download the completed CSC application form.
Step 4: Complete NJU International Student Portal application and upload all notarized academic credentials, physical exam, and police certificate.
Step 5: Pay the NJU application fee (RMB 600) online via UnionPay, WeChat, or international credit card.
Step 6: School-level academic committee reviews dossiers and conducts online technical interviews (February - March).
Step 7: NJU nominates shortlisted candidates to the China Scholarship Council in Beijing for final approval (April - May).
Step 8: Final CSC award list announced; official JW201 visa form and NJU admission notice dispatched (June - July).
Step 9: Apply for Chinese X1 Student Visa at Chinese Visa Application Service Centre (Gerry's) in Pakistan and arrive in Nanjing in September.

application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic CV detailing education history, published papers, academic awards, technical programming skillsets, and referee details.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: SYSU International Student System & CSC Online Application System (Agency No. 10558)
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Submit application on the CSC portal choosing Program Category B (Agency No. 10558 for SYSU), then submit on the SYSU International Student Application System, upload all supporting documents, and pay CNY 400 fee.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Contact potential SYSU faculty supervisors and request a Foreigner Acceptance Letter.
Step 2: Obtain valid English proficiency test or MOI certificate, Foreigner Physical Examination report, and police character certificate.
Step 3: Register on CSC portal (studyinchina.csc.edu.cn), choose Type B, enter SYSU Agency No. 10558, and submit application.
Step 4: Register on SYSU portal (iso.sysu.edu.cn), complete online application, upload all documents including CSC form, and pay CNY 400 fee.
Step 5: SYSU academic departments review dossiers and conduct virtual interviews for shortlisted candidates.
Step 6: University nominates selected candidates to the China Scholarship Council for final approval.
Step 7: CSC issues official Admission Notice and JW201 Visa Form in July.
Step 8: Apply for Chinese X1 Visa at Chinese Visa Center and travel to Guangzhou/Shenzhen for September registration.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated University Recommendation Track (CSC Type B): Admission and scholarship are processed concurrently by SYSU and confirmed by CSC.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Uploaded directly by candidate as signed and stamped official PDF letters from full professors or associate professors.

application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Comprehensive research proposal outlining research domain, methodologies, experimental designs, and alignment with SYSU laboratory facilities.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Standard academic research CV detailing education, publications, research projects, technical skills, and academic awards.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Departmental faculty panel interview via Tencent Meeting / VooV / Zoom evaluating subject knowledge and research aptitude.

step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Browse UMPSA research groups and reach out to prospective supervisors with CV and research draft.

Step 6: IPS issues official Letter of Offer and GRS Appointment Letter.

Step 6: Tongji Graduate School nominates successful candidates to CSC / Shanghai Municipal Education Commission.

Step 8: Apply for Chinese X1 Visa at Chinese Visa Center and arrive in Shanghai for September registration.

step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Identify and email prospective Tsukuba academic advisors with CV, transcripts, and research proposal (October-November).
Step 2: Participate in informal interview and obtain signed Letter of Provisional Acceptance.
Step 3: Complete MEXT University Recommendation application form and compile certified dossiers (December-January).
Step 4: Prospective supervisor submits internal nomination dossier to Tsukuba Graduate School Selection Board.
Step 5: University conducts internal screening and submits institutional recommendation list to MEXT Tokyo (March).
Step 6: MEXT Tokyo officially ratifies scholarship nominations (June).
Step 7: University issues Certificate of Eligibility (COE) and flight e-tickets; apply for Japanese visa at embassy.
Step 8: Fly to Tokyo Narita/Haneda in late September and start autumn semester on October 1.

misleading_claims_debunked: Myth: Japanese language fluency is mandatory. Reality: All STEM graduate programs at Tsukuba are conducted entirely in English.

official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial blogs suggest age limit can be relaxed; MEXT statutory age cutoff (born on or after April 2, 1991) is strictly enforced without exception.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: UMT Graduate School Online Application Portal
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Contact prospective supervisor, obtain acceptance form, register on UMT e-admission portal, submit postgraduate application, upload credentials, and pay RM 150 fee.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Explore UMT faculty expertise directory and email prospective supervisors with CV and research draft.
Step 2: Secure signed Supervisor Acceptance & Research Assistantship Recommendation Form.
Step 3: Register on UMT e-admission portal and complete online postgraduate application.
Step 4: Upload attested academic transcripts, research proposal, passport copy, and English proof.
Step 5: Faculty Graduate Committee reviews technical proposal and conducts online interview.
Step 6: UMT Graduate School issues official Letter of Offer and Scholarship Award Letter.
Step 7: Apply for EMGS Visa Approval Letter (VAL) and Single Entry Visa at Malaysian High Commission in Islamabad.
Step 8: Travel to Terengganu, complete on-campus medical checkup, and matriculate.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: Yenching Academy Online Application Portal
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the Yenching Academy admissions portal, choose your research concentration, upload personal statement, research proposal, transcripts, and register academic referees.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Check whether your home university is a Yenching Partner Institution (if yes, seek internal nomination; if no, apply via Open Application).
Step 2: Draft personal statement (maximum 750 words) and China-focused research proposal (maximum 1,500 words).
Step 3: Secure two academic letters of recommendation from professors who know your work intimately.
Step 4: Submit complete online application before the strict early-December deadline.
Step 5: International Admissions Committee conducts preliminary dossier screening.
Step 6: Shortlisted candidates invited for a 25-30 minute virtual panel interview in January/February.
Step 7: Final offer notifications sent out in late March / early April.
Step 8: Complete Peking University international student enrollment, obtain JW202/visa, and arrive in Beijing in late August.

application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Research proposal (maximum 1,500 words excluding bibliography) detailing a proposed China-focused academic inquiry within your chosen research track.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Professional 1 to 2 page CV detailing academic background, leadership roles, publications, honors, and language skills.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Highly rigorous 25 to 30 minute video interview conducted by a multidisciplinary panel of Peking University professors and international scholars.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS 7.0+, TOEFL 100+, or official proof of English-medium undergraduate instruction accepted.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Certified transcripts and degree certificates; HEC and MoFA attestations required upon formal matriculation.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Review GSFS faculty directory, contact prospective supervisor, receive informal acceptance, complete UTokyo GSFS online application, upload ADB-JSP required forms and income tax documents.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Contact a prospective academic advisor at UTokyo GSFS by October/November and secure informal consent.
Step 2: Compile ADB-JSP application form, employment certificate proving 2+ years full-time experience, and annual family income certification.
Step 3: Submit online admission application to UTokyo GSFS indicating ADB-JSP scholarship interest by December 10.
Step 4: Send certified physical application documents to GSFS Student Affairs Team by postal mail.
Step 5: GSFS faculty committee conducts academic evaluation and shortlisting.
Step 6: UTokyo nominates shortlisted candidates to the Asian Development Bank (ADB) Headquarters in Manila in March.
Step 7: ADB Board officially ratifies scholarship recipients in June.
Step 8: Obtain Japanese visa and arrive in Japan for late September orientation and October 1 matriculation.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: Tokyo Tech Online Admissions System & IGP-A Portal
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Contact prospective academic supervisor, obtain consent, register on Tokyo Tech online application system, submit electronic dossier, and send certified physical documents if requested.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Contact prospective academic advisor at Tokyo Tech with CV, transcripts, and research proposal (August-October).
Step 2: Obtain formal consent from professor to serve as your academic supervisor.
Step 3: Register on Tokyo Tech online application system during the IGP-A application window (September - December).
Step 4: Upload all required documents including MEXT application form and research plan.
Step 5: Departmental admissions committee reviews dossiers and conducts online technical interviews.
Step 6: Tokyo Tech submits institutional nomination list to MEXT Tokyo in March.
Step 7: MEXT Tokyo officially confirms scholarship recipients in June.
Step 8: Receive Certificate of Eligibility, apply for Japanese visa, and arrive in Tokyo in late September for October 1 entry.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated University Recommendation Track (IGP-A): Admission and MEXT scholarship are processed concurrently as a single unified nomination.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by recommenders or uploaded as signed letters from university deans/professors on institutional stationery.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Field of Study and Research Program Plan (Kenkyu Keikakusho) detailing research background, objectives, experimental methods, and contributions.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Structured technical proposal detailing problem statement, literature background, experimental design, and timeline.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic research CV detailing education, technical proficiencies, laboratory skills, and publication history.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Online technical interview via Zoom conducted by prospective supervisor and departmental faculty panel.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 85+, or English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate accepted.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Certified true copies of transcripts and degree certificates; HEC and MoFA attestations recommended for Pakistani credentials.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English or Japanese translation for all non-English/non-Japanese documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Online submission via Tokyo Tech admissions system.

basic_details.scholarship_name: Seoul National University (SNU) Global Scholarship
basic_details.offering_entity: Seoul National University (SNU) Office of International Affairs (OIA)
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: Seoul National University (Gwanak Main Campus and Yeongeon Medical Campus, Seoul, South Korea)
basic_details.major_restrictions: Open to all graduate colleges: College of Engineering, College of Natural Sciences, College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Graduate School of Data Science, College of Pharmacy, College of Medicine, College of Social Sciences, and Graduate School of International Studies (GSIS).
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~160 to 200 graduate scholars supported per semester across Global Scholarship Category 1 (Tuition + Stipend) and Category 2 (Tuition Exemption)
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open international merit competition; Pakistani graduate researchers in STEM, computing, and life sciences secure ~10 to 18 awards per semester
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: Up to 1 year renewable (up to 2 years for Master's, 3 years for PhD) subject to maintaining a minimum semester GPA of 3.0 / 4.3

nationality_requirements: International applicants whose parents are not citizens of South Korea (Pakistan eligible)
eligibility_requirements.age_limit_notes: No formal age limit, but competitive applicants are typically under 35 (Master's) or under 40 (PhD).
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: A recognized 4-year Bachelor's degree (16 years education) for Master's; recognized Master's degree (18 years education) for PhD from an HEC-recognized institution with distinguished academic performance (minimum 75% aggregate or CGPA 3.30 / 4.00; competitive admits typically 3.60+ / 4.00 or top 10% class rank).
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Transcript grades evaluated on SNU 4.3 grading scale; applicants should hold an equivalent of B+ (3.3/4.3) or higher.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Prior degree closely aligned with the applied academic discipline.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Students in their final semester can apply conditionally with a bonafide letter from their university stating expected graduation date.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Research laboratory experience, coding proficiency, or published papers in international journals significantly enhance selection odds.
eligibility_requirements.language_notes: TOEFL iBT min 80, IELTS Academic min 6.0, TEPS min 269, or official English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate from Pakistani university confirming undergraduate/master education was conducted in English.
eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: Korean proficiency (TOPIK) is not required for English-track STEM programs; TOPIK Level 3+ recommended for Humanities and Social Sciences.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Applicants can apply for the SNU Global Scholarship during the general international graduate admissions application window or upon admission.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Cannot concurrently hold other full external government scholarships (e.g. GKS/KGSP).

tuition_fee.details: Full tuition fee waiver for the enrolled academic semester/year (KRW 3,200,000 to 6,100,000 / semester value depending on college).

admission_application_fee.details: SNU international graduate admissions application fee of KRW 90,000 (~USD 68; ~PKR 18,900) paid online via UwayApply.

accommodation.details: SNU Gwanak Residence Halls (Bldg 900-906) provided at highly subsidized student rates: KRW 200,000 to 350,000 / month (~USD 150 to 260 / month) for double/single rooms, easily covered from the monthly stipend.

monthly_stipend.details: Global Scholarship Category 1 recipients receive a tax-free monthly living stipend of KRW 1,200,000 / month (~USD 900 / month; ~PKR 252,000 / month) for 12 months. Supplementary laboratory research assistantship (RA) stipends typically add KRW 600,000 to 1,000,000 / month.

airfare.details: Selected Global Scholarship 1 awardees receive a one-time economy round-trip or one-way flight subsidy (up to KRW 1,000,000; ~USD 750).

visa_fee.details: Korean D-2 Student Visa processing fees at the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Islamabad are paid by the student.

health_insurance.details: Mandatory Korean National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) covers foreign students; subsidized monthly premium is ~KRW 70,000 / month, covered from the monthly living stipend.

food_allowance.details: SNU campus cafeterias (Student Center cafeteria, Dormitory cafeteria, and Halal-friendly meal options) provide wholesome meals for KRW 3,500 to 6,000 per meal; easily covered by the KRW 1,200,000 monthly stipend.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Comprehensive access to SNU Main Library, digital archives, supercomputing facilities, and advanced laboratory equipment.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Laboratory BK21 (Brain Korea 21 Four) funding and National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) grants provide travel funding for international conferences.

travel_transit_allowance.details: Seoul Metropolitan subway and bus transit (T-Money card) paid from monthly stipend (~KRW 60,000/month).

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: SNU Graduate Admissions Portal & UwayApply
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Create an applicant account on UwayApply during the open application window, select Seoul National University Graduate International Admissions (Track 1), complete data entry, and check the scholarship application box for the SNU Global Scholarship.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Contact prospective SNU professors to discuss lab openings and research alignment (June - July for Spring, December - January for Fall).
Step 2: Create account on UwayApply and complete the SNU International Graduate Admissions form.
Step 3: Indicate interest and complete the application section for the SNU Global Scholarship.
Step 4: Pay the application fee of KRW 90,000 online via international credit card.
Step 5: Have academic recommenders submit online recommendation letters directly through the automated email system.
Step 6: Upload or courier certified documents (transcripts, degrees, apostille/consular confirmation, family relations proof).
Step 7: Departmental admissions committee reviews applications and conducts technical interviews via Zoom (September for Spring, April for Fall).
Step 8: Final admission and Global Scholarship results announced by SNU OIA (November for Spring, June for Fall).
Step 9: Receive Certificate of Admission (CoA), apply for Korean D-2 visa in Islamabad, and matriculate at SNU.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated Application: Scholarship consideration is embedded directly within the SNU general graduate admissions process.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by referees via the secure SNU recommendation portal link generated upon application fee payment.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Self-Introduction and Study Plan covering personal background, motivations for studying at SNU, undergraduate research achievements, and proposed graduate research project.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Structured plan detailing research problem, methodologies, expected academic contributions, and alignment with target SNU laboratory.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Standard academic CV highlighting academic honors, research papers, software projects, and technical skills.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Online video interview via Zoom conducted by a 2-3 faculty member committee assessing domain knowledge, mathematical/analytical skills, and research drive.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: Not required; GRE is optional but strongly recommended for competitive STEM applicants.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Degrees and transcripts must be authenticated by HEC Pakistan, MoFA, and consular legalized by the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Islamabad, or apostilled.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English translation required for all non-English documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Online application via UwayApply followed by submission of verified hardcopy credentials as instructed by the admissions office.

official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial forums state that professor contact is not required; in practice, STEM applicants without prior professor contact rarely get allocated lab space or scholarship funding.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must maintain a minimum semester GPA of 3.0 / 4.3 (Grade B equivalent) to retain the scholarship for subsequent semesters.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Semester-end academic record review by the Office of International Affairs (OIA) before releasing subsequent tuition waivers and stipends.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Part-time work permitted up to 20 hours/week during semester with university and immigration permission, but full-time external employment is prohibited.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: No obligation to return to Pakistan; graduates can transition to Korean D-10 job seeker visas or E-7 professional work visas.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.service_obligations_or_bonds: No bond or mandatory service agreement.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Scholarship cancelled if the student is subject to disciplinary action, withdraws without authorization, or fails to meet minimum GPA standards.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_university: Transferring to another university results in immediate loss of SNU scholarship benefits.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Changing majors requires formal review and typically results in loss of the Global Scholarship funding.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Global Scholarship duration is strictly capped at standard program length (up to 4 semesters for Master's, 6-8 for PhD); subsequent extensions must be funded via lab RA/TA funds.

step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Explore KAIST departmental research laboratories and contact prospective professors with CV and research interests (July for Spring / December for Fall).

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: UNIST Graduate Admissions Online Portal
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the UNIST admissions portal, complete online application form, upload personal statement and transcripts, pay USD 50 fee, and dispatch certified physical documents to UNIST Admissions Office.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Contact prospective UNIST professors in target research areas with CV and research interests (July-August for Spring / December-January for Fall).
Step 2: Register on UNIST Graduate Admissions Online System during open intake.
Step 3: Complete online application, upload documents, and pay USD 50 fee.
Step 4: Register two academic recommenders who submit evaluation letters online.
Step 5: Send certified hard-copy documents (degrees, transcripts, apostille/attestation) via DHL to UNIST Admissions Office in Ulsan.
Step 6: Departmental faculty committee reviews dossiers and conducts virtual technical interviews.
Step 7: Final admission and scholarship award results announced online.
Step 8: Obtain Certificate of Admission (CoA), apply for South Korean D-2 visa, and arrive in Ulsan.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated Institutional Route: Admission and scholarship funding are decided together based on departmental faculty recommendation.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by two academic recommenders via confidential portal links.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Personal Statement and Study Plan (prescribed UNIST format) describing motivation, research experiences, scholarly interests, and post-graduation goals.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Structured research plan detailing proposed technical investigations, methodologies, and alignment with target UNIST laboratories.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic research CV detailing education, laboratory proficiencies, software skills, and publication history.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Online technical interview via Zoom conducted by prospective supervisor and departmental faculty panel.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 80+, TOEIC 800+, or English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate accepted.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: HEC and MoFA Pakistan attestations required, followed by Korean Embassy consular legalization in Islamabad or Apostille.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English or Korean translation for all non-English/non-Korean documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Dual submission: Online portal application followed by mandatory postal dispatch of certified physical dossier to UNIST.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: GIST Online Graduate Admissions System
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the GIST admissions portal, complete online application form (no application fee charged), upload personal statement and transcripts, and dispatch certified physical documents to Section of International Admissions.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Contact prospective GIST professors in target research areas with CV and research interests (July-August for Spring / December-January for Fall).
Step 2: Register on GIST Online Graduate Admissions System during open intake.
Step 3: Complete online application and upload documents (application fee is completely free).
Step 4: Register two academic recommenders who submit evaluation letters online.
Step 5: Send certified hard-copy documents (degrees, transcripts, apostille/attestation) via DHL to GIST International Admissions in Gwangju.
Step 6: Departmental faculty committee reviews dossiers and conducts virtual technical interviews.
Step 7: Final admission and scholarship award results announced online.
Step 8: Obtain Certificate of Admission (CoA), apply for South Korean D-2 visa, and arrive in Gwangju (flight reimbursement processed upon arrival).

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: NUS Graduate Admission System (GDA3)
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the NUS GDA3 portal, select PhD programme of choice, indicate scholarship application, upload research proposal, CV, transcripts, test scores, and register two academic referees.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Explore NUS faculty research groups and contact prospective supervisors with research abstract (September-October).
Step 2: Register on NUS Graduate Admission System (GDA3) during the open application window (October to December for August intake).
Step 3: Complete online application, upload all documents, and pay SGD 50-100 application fee.
Step 4: Referees submit letters of recommendation electronically through the portal.
Step 5: Departmental admissions committee reviews applications and conducts technical interviews (January-February).
Step 6: Department nominates top candidates to the NUS Graduate School PGF Selection Committee.
Step 7: PGF offers announced in March/April.
Step 8: Accept offer, complete Singapore Student's Pass formalities, and matriculate in early August.

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: HKU Online Application System for Research Postgraduate Programs
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the HKU graduate admissions portal, select PhD program, complete application form, upload personal statement and transcripts, pay HKD 400 fee, and register two recommenders.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Explore HKU faculty research profiles and contact prospective supervisors with CV and research abstract (September-October).
Step 2: Register on HKU Online Application System during open intake (September to December).
Step 3: Complete online application, upload documents, and pay HKD 400 application fee.
Step 4: Referees submit evaluation letters online via confidential portal links.
Step 5: Departmental admissions committee reviews applications and conducts technical interviews via Zoom.
Step 6: Department nominates top candidates to the Graduate School Presidential Fellowship Selection Panel.
Step 7: Official admission and HKU Presidential PhD Fellowship award letter issued in January/February.
Step 8: Accept offer, apply for Hong Kong Student Visa via HKU, and arrive in Hong Kong in late August.

application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Structured research proposal (2-4 pages) detailing problem formulation, methodology, literature review, and anticipated scientific contributions.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Comprehensive academic CV detailing publications, research projects, technical skills, and honors.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Online technical interview via Zoom conducted by prospective supervisor and departmental doctoral admission committee.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic 6.5+ or TOEFL iBT 85+ required; GRE is optional but recommended.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Certified true copies of transcripts and degree certificates; HEC attestation required for Pakistani credentials upon enrollment.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified official English translation for all non-English documents.

step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Check eligibility for RTG King's (SET/SOM), Queen's (SERD), or Loom Nam Khong fellowship categories.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Identify target international program, download Non-ASEAN scholarship application form, submit admission and scholarship dossier to the program coordinator/faculty by the deadline.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Check target international graduate program at Chulalongkorn University and contact program coordinator.
Step 2: Complete the Application Form for Graduate Scholarship Programme for Non-ASEAN Countries.
Step 3: Compile transcripts, degree certificates, research proposal, medical certificate, CV, and English test scores.
Step 4: Submit complete application dossier to the relevant Faculty/Program at Chulalongkorn University before the faculty deadline (typically February-March).
Step 5: Faculty evaluates academic credentials and conducts online technical interviews.
Step 6: Faculty selects top candidates and nominates them to the University Scholarship Committee.
Step 7: Office of International Affairs issues official award notification in May.
Step 8: Receive admission letter, apply for Thai Non-Immigrant ED Visa at Thai Embassy in Islamabad, and book flight provided by Chulalongkorn.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated Faculty-to-University Route: Application submitted directly to target faculty, which screens applicants and forwards nominations to central university scholarship board.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted as two confidential recommendation letters signed by university professors in sealed envelopes or sent directly via official institutional email.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Statement of Purpose describing academic background, research interests, career vision, and why Chulalongkorn University is the desired destination.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Structured research proposal (2-4 pages) detailing problem formulation, methodology, literature review, and anticipated contributions.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Comprehensive academic CV detailing education, laboratory techniques, research publications, and awards.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Online technical interview via Zoom conducted by prospective supervisor and departmental doctoral admission committee.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic 6.0+, TOEFL iBT 79+, CU-TEP 75+, or English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate accepted.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Certified true copies of transcripts and degree certificates; HEC and MoFA attestations recommended for Pakistani credentials.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified official English translation for all non-English documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Submission of application dossier to target faculty/program graduate office.

selection_process_and_weights.academic_weight: 35% (Prior CGPA, academic consistency in STEM fields)
selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 35% (Research proposal rigor, engineering problem solving, and technical depth)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 5% (Clarity of vision and alignment with faculty priorities)
selection_process_and_weights.interview_weight: 10% (Technical interview performance with prospective supervisor and faculty panel)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: Faculty Graduate Committee, School Deans, and Chulalongkorn University Scholarship Selection Board.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Two-stage evaluation: departmental technical vetting of research alignment followed by central university award confirmation.

competitiveness_profile.total_annual_applicants: ~800 to 1,200 non-ASEAN applicants across faculties
competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~50 to 80 Non-ASEAN scholarship awards annually
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~10.0% to 14.0% for candidates with strong engineering/science backgrounds and CGPA >= 3.55
competitiveness_profile.typical_successful_applicant_gpa: Undergraduate/Master's CGPA >= 3.55 / 4.00, accompanied by strong laboratory foundations
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Graduates in chemical engineering, petroleum, materials, computing, or pharmaceutical sciences with solid research proposals.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates from top Pakistani universities (NUST, UET Lahore, NED Karachi, Quaid-i-Azam, FAST-NUCES, COMSATS).
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Egypt, Nigeria, Russia, Turkey.

fake_websites_and_scams: Only apply through official portals academic.chula.ac.th and inter.chula.ac.th.
Chulalongkorn does not work with third-party agents; all applications must be submitted directly to target faculties.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Faculty application processing fee of THB 1,000 is paid directly through secure university banking channels.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Commercial agency written proposals are rejected; applicants must write their own research proposals.
hidden_costs_breakdown: Application fee: THB 1,000 (~PKR 7,500).
Thai Student Visa fee in Pakistan: ~PKR 15,000.
HEC document attestation in Pakistan: ~PKR 10,000 to 15,000.
Initial pocket money before first stipend cycle: ~THB 10,000 (~PKR 75,000).
misleading_claims_debunked: Myth: Thai language is required. Reality: All international programs at Chulalongkorn are conducted 100% in English.
Myth: Flights are self-funded. Reality: The Non-ASEAN scholarship explicitly covers economy class round-trip international airfare.
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial sites suggest accommodation is not funded; the scholarship provides a dedicated THB 7,000/month accommodation allowance.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Maintain minimum semester GPA of 3.25 out of 4.00 throughout degree study.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time physical research presence at Chulalongkorn campus; residence at CU iHouse or nearby university housing.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Semi-annual progress report evaluated by academic advisor and presented to Graduate School.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Scholars may not engage in outside employment during the study period.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None; scholars are free to seek international careers, postdoc opportunities, or industrial employment globally upon graduation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.service_obligations_or_bonds: Zero national service bond.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Termination of scholarship if GPA falls below required standard or for academic misconduct.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Field of study cannot be changed after enrollment.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Maximum tenure is 2 years (Master's) and 3 years (PhD); extensions are generally not funded by the scholarship.
